fact: Media Rights Agenda reports that the Freedom of Information Act, 2011 is in force and gives a right of access to information held by public bodies, as shown by a Federal High Court judgment enforcing it in 2026; the year 2011 is the Act's year as named in the report.

A Federal High Court in Lagos (Justice Aneke) ruled on 24 February 2026, in a suit on a journalist's October 2020 request, that the Nigeria Shippers Council breached the Freedom of Information Act and ordered it to disclose the information or give reasons for withholding it.

The Federal High Court, Abuja, applies the Freedom of Information Act, 2011 as the specific, operative access to information legislation, taking precedence over the Petroleum Industry Act where they conflict.

In suit FHC/ABJ/CS/1631/2023 the Federal High Court, Abuja, held NNPCL a public institution under the FOI Act and ordered it by mandamus to supply the information HEDA Resources Centre had requested on a $3 billion crude-for-cash loan.

This document is the text of the Freedom of Information Act, 2011, passed by both Houses on 24 May 2011 and assented to by President Jonathan on 28 May 2011; it establishes a right of any person to request information held by public institutions.
The Global Data Barometer report lists freedom of information legislation among the transparency reforms Nigeria has adopted over the past two decades.
